source.note: supportWindows transcribed from content/docs/releases/README.md at the pinned ref: the 'Currently supported releases' table's Supported Kubernetes column (1.20, 1.21) plus the 'Old cert-manager releases' table's Compatible Kubernetes column (0.11 through 1.19). SUPPORTED was chosen over the narrower TESTED column deliberately: supported is the vendor's own commitment ('we will still respond to and fix any bug reports for that version'), tested only what their kind-based e2e matrix happens to cover. The matrix lives in the cert-manager/website repo, NOT cert-manager/cert-manager — the code repo publishes no compatibility table. Floor is 0.11, the oldest row upstream publishes; anything older reports VERSION_NOT_IN_CATALOG (honest 'no vendor data'). The 1.12 row (1.22-1.32) is WIDER than 1.13's (1.21-1.27): 1.12 was a two-year commercial LTS whose window kept growing after 1.13 shipped — transcribed faithfully, ceilings are not monotonic across versions. upgradeNotes is EMPTY BY DESIGN since 2026-09-09: cert-manager's breaking changes moved out of this catalog and into the generated-rule pipeline (kb/cert-manager -> k8s-rules/cert-manager), the same move Argo CD, Karpenter and Traefik made. The catalog now carries the support matrix ONLY, and the hop it produces (K8S_SUPPORT) is what selects those rules; AddonCompatAnalyzer.forcedHop is deliberately independent of upgradeNotes so emptying this list does not silence the add-on. The knowledge base is extracted from content/docs/releases/upgrading/upgrading-<a.b>-<c.d>.md at THIS SAME REF, filed under the TARGET minor <c.d>; upgrading-1.12.md (the LTS guide) is filed under 1.13. The versioned doc snapshots (content/v1.1X-docs/) were compared against content/docs/ at this ref: only v1.15-docs differs, in upgrading-1.3-1.4.md and upgrading-1.7-1.8.md, neither of which carries a rule — so the single master copy is read for every minor.
